text: Harborline Industrial Supply is a fictional company we'll use to walk through a full approval-process design, start to finish, using only tools from Chapters 1 and 2.
Three complaints, one root cause: deals stalled for days on email approvals, two reps discounting 30% or more unchecked, and finance with no record of who approved what.

That becomes a two-tier design. Entry criteria catches anything submitted over a 10% discount. Ten to twenty-five percent goes to the owner's manager; anything deeper goes to the Sales Director. The record locks the moment it enters the process.
Here's the process as it would actually be configured: entry criteria, two approval steps by severity, and final actions that update status, unlock the record, and notify the owner on rejection.

Locking isn't an afterthought. It stops a rep from changing the discount while the old number is still under review, and unlocking happens only in the two final actions -- never while a decision is still pending.
Every decision now lands automatically in the quote's approval history. Next up: the same design method applied to a time-based problem instead of a dollar threshold -- service level escalation.
